summary: mountainash-settings eliminates configuration boilerplate for Python data applications. One base class, any config source, typed credentials, and a built-in secrets layer — no more scattered os.environ calls or home-rolled config parsers.

concepts.name: Pydantic settings done right
evidence: Extends pydantic-settings BaseSettings — full field validation, type coercion, and IDE autocomplete
YAML, TOML, JSON, and .env files all in one place via config_files=[...]
Template syntax: log_file = 'logs/{APP_NAME}/{RUNDATE}.log' — fields populate each other

concepts.name: Smart caching for data pipelines
evidence: get_settings() returns the same instance on every call for the same config — no redundant I/O or env reads
Runtime overrides (e.g. passing a batch ID at call time) never pollute the cache — each override gets a model_copy()

concepts.name: Declarative connection profiles
evidence: Define a ProfileDescriptor once — pydantic fields, auth union, and template wiring are installed automatically
descriptor_invariants_for() gives free pytest coverage for every registered profile

concepts.name: 12 typed auth modes, zero glue code
evidence: Covers PasswordAuth, TokenAuth, JWTAuth, OAuth2Auth, OAuth1Auth, OAuth2AuthCodeAuth, IAMAuth, AzureADAuth, WindowsAuth, KerberosAuth, CertificateAuth, ServiceAccountAuth, NoAuth
All are pydantic models — validated, type-safe, SecretStr-protected
auth_to_driver_kwargs() converts to driver kwargs in one call

concepts.name: Pluggable secrets backend
evidence: Register any secrets provider (AWS SSM, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault) as a single callable
'secret:path/to/value' in your YAML or env vars — automatically resolved before pydantic validation
Works in nested pydantic model fields and auth specs

documentation_plan: One-paragraph product pitch with before/after code snippet
Feature bullet list: typed config, multi-format files, template fields, connection profiles, 12 auth modes, secrets layer
